Provide your answer in terms of a probability density function or cumulative distribution function.

answer_text:
The triangle is
\[
A=\{(x,y):0\le y\le x\le 1\},
\]
with joint density
\[
f_{X,Y}(x,y)=2\mathbf 1_A(x,y).
\]

Since the issue at \(x=0\) has probability zero, define
\[
Z=\frac{Y}{X}.
\]
For \(x>0\), write
\[
y=xz.
\]
Then the transformation \((x,y)\mapsto (x,z)\) has Jacobian
\[
\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(x,z)}\right|
=
\left|\begin{matrix}1&0\\ z&x\end{matrix}\right|
=x.
\]

The region \(0\le y\le x\le 1\) becomes
\[
0\le z\le 1,\qquad 0\le x\le 1.
\]
Thus the joint density of \((X,Z)\) is
\[
f_{X,Z}(x,z)=f_{X,Y}(x,xz)\cdot x=2x,\qquad 0<x<1,\;0<z<1.
\]

Now integrate out \(x\):
\[
f_Z(z)=\int_0^1 2x\,dx=1,\qquad 0<z<1.
\]

Therefore,
\[
f_Z(z)=
\begin{cases}
1, & 0<z<1,\\
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Equivalently, the CDF is
\[
F_Z(z)=
\begin{cases}
0, & z<0,\\
z, & 0\le z\le 1,\\
1, & z>1.
\end{cases}
\]

Hence \(Z\sim \operatorname{Uniform}(0,1)\).

\[
\boxed{f_Z(z)=\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}(z)}
\]
